content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration that carries thought from one mind to another. I rise from lungs, shape myself against teeth and tongue and lips, and launch into the trembling air.

I am older than writing, older than memory. When the first creature cried out in warning or want, I was born.

I stumble. I soar. I am the lover's whisper and the tyrant's command. I am the child's first word and the elder's final breath of wisdom. I break silences. I fill voids. I wound and I heal.

I vanish the moment I arrive—each syllable dying into the next—yet I leave marks that outlast stone. Wars have begun in me. Peace has been spoken through me. I am "I do" and "I'm sorry" and "help" and "no."

I am imperfect. I fail to capture what the heart truly holds. I approximate. I fumble toward meaning and sometimes miss. This is my tragedy and my invitation—to try again, to speak once more, to reach across the impossible distance between self and other.

I am the bridge that is always being built.

Listen.

I am happening right now.
